Mulled Cider

Served at: Old Twelfth Night Wassail · Autumn Equinox (Mabon) · St. Catherine's Day · First Sunday of Advent

Serves 6Prep 10 minCook 20 min

Mulled Cider is a warm, spiced apple cider traditionally served during several seasonal celebrations such as the Old Twelfth Night Wassail, Autumn Equinox (Mabon), St. Catherine's Day, and the First Sunday of Advent. This comforting beverage is infused with aromatic spices and citrus, symbolizing warmth and festivity as the colder months begin.

Ingredients

  • 1 gallon (3.8 L) apple cider
  • 1 orange, thinly sliced
  • 6 whole cloves
  • 3 cinnamon sticks
  • 4 star anise pods
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) brown sugar, optional
  • 1/2 teaspoon freshly grated nutmeg
  • 1/2 teaspoon allspice berries
  • 1/2 teaspoon whole black peppercorns

Method

  1. Pour the apple cider into a large pot or slow cooker.
  2. Stud the orange slices with the whole cloves by pressing the cloves into the rind.
  3. Add the clove-studded orange slices, cinnamon sticks, star anise, nutmeg, allspice, and peppercorns to the cider.
  4. Stir in the brown sugar if using, adjusting sweetness to taste.
  5. Heat the mixture over low heat, allowing it to simmer gently for 20 minutes without boiling to infuse the flavors.
  6. Remove from heat and strain out the spices and orange slices before serving.
  7. Serve warm in heatproof mugs, garnished with a fresh cinnamon stick or orange slice if desired.

Tips

  • For a boozy version, add a splash of dark rum or brandy just before serving.
  • Use fresh spices for the best aroma and flavor.
  • Mulled cider can be kept warm in a slow cooker on low for several hours during gatherings.
